newsitem.title: UK: Ad agencies urged to compete with consultants.
newsitem.headline: Ad agencies urged to compete with consultants.

text.p: Advertising agencies are facing more competition from management consultants and from small creative "hot shops" capable of generating ideas and commercials quickly and cheaply, said Martin Sorrell head of WPP Group Plc.

"We face new competition from the established but ambitious management consultancies and we face competition of another kind from companies capable of generating ideas and design and promotions and commercials at a speed and a cost far closer to that of newspapers and broadcasting than to the stately deliberations of conventional advertising agencies," Sorrell said in a speech.
As an example of the latter, Sorrell cited the Creative Artists Agency -- a Hollywood-based talent agency that is creating advertising for Coca-Cola in the United States.

He said in his speech late on Wednesday at the Design and Art Directors' President's lecture that "the only way for agencies to get back up the value chain and to regain their strategic ground is not to forsake their creative heritage -- but to build on it".
Sorrell, the head of the world's largest marketing services group, said, "If we don't do it, someone else will -- and they are probably called Spielberg or Disney."
He said ad agencies had become more specialised in the last 30 years in the forms of creativity they offered and that made them more narrowly focused and more limited.

"There was once a time when client companies would welcome an agency's thoughts on just about all aspects of their business: diversification, brand strategy, investment, internal training, presentation -- as well as advertising and promotions," Sorrell said.
But that had changed, at least in the United States and Britain, and clients expected -- and agencies were only able to provide -- creativity in their communications, Sorrell said.
